entries.name: WHATWG HTML reference regex for a valid e-mail address (ASCII only)
entries.source_title: HTML Living Standard, 4.10.5.1.5 E-mail state, 'valid e-mail address'
entries.accepts_note: Long ASCII TLDs and xn-- A-labels pass; only Unicode is rejected.
entries.note: The spec's own prose allows Unicode in the definition it introduces; its reference regex restricts every character class to ASCII. Measured 2026-09-24 on representative values.

entries.accepts_note: Long ASCII TLDs and xn-- A-labels pass.
entries.note: Score 3,555 on 2026-09-24 (Stack Exchange API, /questions/201323/answers sorted by votes). Measured 2026-09-24.

entries.name: regular-expressions.info 'simple' email regex (ASCII only, letters-only TLD)
entries.source_title: Jan Goyvaerts, 'How to Find or Validate an Email Address'
entries.accepts_note: Long ASCII TLDs pass; xn-- TLDs fail on the letters-only final label.
entries.note: Page text: 'the one you'll find right on this site's home page: \b[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}\b. This regular expression, I claim, matches any email address.' The same page states it does not support internationalized domains. Measured 2026-09-24 with the i flag.
